Follow `RULES.md` strictly. Repo tooling and explicit user instructions win conflicts. `RULES.md` defines definition of done, formatting/lint, warnings-as-errors, tests/coverage, and code size/complexity budgets. `WORKFLOW.md` defines repository workflow. `RELEASING.md` defines release rules.

For concrete requests, start with relevant files; otherwise inspect top-level docs, manifests, and module READMEs. Do not assume module scope. Read every file you modify in full before editing. Do not remove, rename, or downgrade intentional functionality unless the user explicitly asked. Do not “fix” dependency or type problems by deleting behavior or weakening checks. Keep diffs tight. Run repository validation commands after changes. Do not bypass hooks, checks, or validation steps. Never use `--no-verify`.

Never commit unless the user explicitly asks. If committing, commit only files changed in this session. Use explicit paths when staging. Never use broad staging commands that can capture other agents’ work. Before committing, run `git status` and verify only intended files are staged.
`git add <specific-file-paths>`
`git pull --rebase`
`git reset --hard`
`git clean -fd`
`git commit --no-verify`

Protect other agents’ changes. Resolve conflicts only in files you changed. If a conflict appears in untouched files, stop and ask the user. Read full issues including comments. Analyze PRs before local changes. Do not open PRs unless the user explicitly asked. Do not merge or close anything unless the user explicitly asked. Keep responses concise, direct, and technical. No emojis in commits, issues, PR comments, or code comments unless explicitly asked.

Store transient context under `.llm/{DIR}/`; do not use `.context/`. Treat `.llm/` as disposable working state; promote durable documentation explicitly.
